_comment: Load-bearing claims only. The audit found 1,197 numeric claims across the base; retrofitting all of them is busywork. These are the ones a live position or a stated conclusion actually rests on -- if one of these is wrong, a decision changes. Every entry carries how it was obtained and how confident I am that it is right, which is NOT the same question. status: verified (I pulled it from the primary source myself) | reported (a secondary source asserts it, I did not verify) | contested (sources disagree and I have not settled it) | unresolved (I flagged it and never closed it).

claims.claim: Nifty FY26 earnings grew 4.5% against 12-15% expected
claims.why_load_bearing: This is the single number that overturned my 'earnings +18%' framing and therefore the entire medium-horizon case. Everything downstream of it changes if it is wrong.
claims.note: The 18% figure was ONE quarter with 60% of the growth from five stocks. The 4.5% is the full-year number.

claims.claim: 4.5% actual versus 6.9% on a reconstituted index
claims.why_load_bearing: Explains WHY Indian consensus misses every year -- survivorship in the index itself. It is the mechanism, not just the observation.

claims.claim: Fed-model ERP has R-squared of 0.5% versus 56.3% for plain P/E
claims.why_load_bearing: Demolished my own ERP chain after I had already given the user three successive ERP numbers. The correction only holds if this holds.
claims.note: Damodaran's rigorous series shows no negative ERP years since 1960, which is a separate and independent check that pointed the same way.

claims.claim: A sub-12-month trade needs ~9.85% more gross return than a 12-month-plus one; 11.8% at high income
claims.obtained: computed in scripts/required_return.py from statutory rates
claims.why_load_bearing: It is the reason the short-horizon sleeve has a higher bar than the medium one. Arithmetic, not opinion.
claims.source: STCG 20% vs LTCG 12.5% + Rs1.25L exemption, Income Tax Act

claims.claim: India -9.9% over 1y and -15.0% over 2y in USD, versus S&P +19.2%
claims.obtained: computed from our own OHLC pulls
claims.why_load_bearing: The rupee is why the local-currency chart flatters the market. Any allocation argument that ignores it is wrong for a global comparison.

claims.claim: India tariff in force is 10% under Section 301(b)/304(a), effective ~2026-07-24, from a 60-country forced-labour investigation initiated 2026-03-12 -- NOT India-specific. ~45% of India's US-bound exports (~$87bn) exempt via Annex I/II. Section 122 Proclamation 11012 bridged from 2026-02-20 (the day IEEPA fell) for its 150-day cap. The 18% came from a bilateral deal under the IEEPA framework struck down nine days later.
claims.obtained: agent research + SCOTUS decision Learning Resources v. Trump, 6-3, 20 Feb 2026
claims.why_load_bearing: I told the user 18% repeatedly. It was wrong. This is the correction and it changes the export-sector maths.
claims.source: 91 FR 47318 doc# 2026-15181 (Sec 301 notice, pub 2026-07-28); 91 FR 47717 doc# 2026-15274 (Presidential Memorandum); 91 FR 9339 doc# 2026-03824 (Proclamation 11012, Sec 122 bridge); 91 FR 18183 doc# 2026-06956 (Proclamation 11020, Sec 232 pharma)
claims.note: Generic pharma is separate: Section 232, 0% from 2026-08-01, 100% Aug 2028, 200% Aug 2029, legally untouched by the IEEPA ruling.

claims.claim: Russia is now >50% of India's crude imports and the discount has narrowed to near-premium
claims.why_load_bearing: Sets the size of the Senate-sanctions tail risk. At >50% it is an index-level risk, not a sector one.

claims.claim: The 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' passed the Senate 86-11 on Friday 7 Aug 2026. NO confirmed House floor vote is scheduled; co-sponsor Blumenthal said on 26 Aug he expects a September vote. The bill grants the President broad waiver authority -- sanctions and tariffs waivable on certification to Congress of national interest.
claims.why_load_bearing: Still the largest tail risk to an Indian book, but SMALLER than recorded. The waiver authority means passage creates an authority rather than an outcome, so the path from a House vote to 100% tariffs on Indian crude buyers runs through a presidential decision, not automatically.
claims.note: CORRECTED 2026-08-29. I had logged a 31 Aug House vote as a dated T+2 catalyst on three-week-old reporting. It is not scheduled. Returned to the undated watch.

claims.claim: SIP and DII flows were double-counted, understating the supply problem by 40%; absorption is 2.15 years at the DII run-rate
claims.obtained: own correction after catching the double-count
claims.why_load_bearing: The supply-absorption argument was the main structural bull case. It is 40% weaker than I said.
claims.note: The underlying SIP series is still CONTESTED: Rs31,961cr vs Rs22,908cr, unresolved.

claims.claim: Conversion of announced capex into actual fixed assets fell from ~40% pre-2011 to 10-15%
claims.obtained: agent research, resolved a three-series contradiction
claims.why_load_bearing: Resolves why announced-capex headlines and actual-investment data disagree. It is the reason L&T-type exposure is a contract-mix question, not a headline question.

claims.claim: India's SPR covers 9.5 days (RTI, March 2026), against an IEA 90-day standard; one-third of facilities empty
claims.why_load_bearing: Determines how much an oil shock actually hurts. The 9.5 vs 60 vs 74 spread is a definitional gap: caverns-only versus mandated refiner stock.
claims.note: Partially resolved -- methodology explains the gap. Not fully closed.

claims.claim: Forward book NET SHORT $103.33bn at 30 June 2026 -- essentially flat vs $103.06bn at 31 March, after widening to $106.7bn in May. Reserves hit an all-time record $729.33bn for the week ended 21 Aug 2026, +$12.42bn w/w. RBI net SOLD ~$8.9bn in April and $6.10bn in May, then net BOUGHT $561mn in June -- the first net-buying month.
claims.obtained: agent research against the WSS series
claims.why_load_bearing: Settles the contested reserves claim and supplies the mechanism behind the rupee's peer-relative weakness found independently from price. A headline stock near its high funded by record intervention is a managed currency, not a strong one.
claims.source: RBI Bulletin Table 4/4A; RBI Weekly Statistical Supplement, week ended 2026-08-21
claims.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-29 -- this was the single most important dark number. The secondary claim that RBI 'trims short forward dollar position to $72.5 billion' is REFUTED against the primary table. The finding that matters: reserves grew roughly $47bn to a fresh record WHILE the forward book stayed pinned near $103bn short. The reserve build did NOT come from unwinding the forward defence, so the headline number still is not evidence the defence ended.

claims.claim: The US is now India's largest remittance source at 27.7%
claims.why_load_bearing: A core strand of the Washington-concentration finding. Remittances were the channel I had assumed was diversified away from the US.
claims.source: RBI Bulletin, 'Changing Dynamics of India's Remittances -- Sixth Round' (survey covering FY2023-24)
claims.note: CORRECTED 2026-08-29. I had demoted this to UNVERIFIABLE after five failed searches. It is REAL and sits in the RBI's own Bulletin verbatim, with a clean multi-round series: 22.9% (2016-17) -> 23.4% -> 27.7% (FY2023-24). The searches failed because the figure lives inside a specifically-titled Bulletin article, not under generic remittance terms. This is the opposite of the failure mode I was guarding against -- a FALSE NEGATIVE, where I buried a true claim because my search strategy was wrong. 'Not found' means not found, not false.

claims.claim: FPI outflows Rs2.87 lakh crore YTD 2026 as of 25 June; net FDI near a record low of $7.65bn against record gross FDI of $95bn
claims.why_load_bearing: Net versus gross FDI is the whole story -- record gross with near-record-low net means repatriation, which reads as an exit, not an entry.

claims.claim: Goods trade deficit $30.43bn in June 2026 (+59.3% YoY), $31.98bn in July, a 6-month high; current account back to a $6.2bn deficit in June
claims.why_load_bearing: The external position is deteriorating while the equity market treats India as a domestic story.

claims.claim: EU CBAM: 15-22% price hit on steel, 41% drop in aluminium exports, $116/tonne by 2034; the India-EU FTA does NOT exempt India
claims.why_load_bearing: An India-EU FTA headline will be read as bullish for metals. It is not, and this is why.

claims.claim: 199 forged Tejas supplier test certificates found by HAL's own audit; 18 fighters with 10 engineless by April 2026; only 7 GE engines delivered against a $1bn deal
claims.why_load_bearing: Closed the HAL position. If the certificate count is wrong the close was still right on the engine number alone, so the decision is robust to this one being off.

claims.claim: MSRDC Rs45cr differential-interest payment; RBI query into the board's own Rs1 lakh penalty on its CEO; US securities class action
claims.why_load_bearing: Closed the MEDIUM and suspended the LONG. Three independent items pointing the same way is what made it decisive rather than any one of them.

claims.claim: Dixon Q1 FY27 operating margin 2.29%, down from 3.04% YoY; revenue +21.1%, operating income -8.6%, net income +194.8% at 1.86x operating income
claims.obtained: own pull of yfinance quarterly financials, computed here
claims.why_load_bearing: Closed the position. Settles the dixon-pat conflict: neither the -36% screen figure nor our +119% TTM figure described what was happening.
claims.note: Sep 2025 quarter missing from the series; does not affect the like-for-like comparison. NOT checked against a company filing.

claims.claim: Q1 FY27, 62 large Indian names: revenue-weighted operating income +1.6% and margin -207bps, but ex three operationally negative names (IOC, BPCL, TMPV) operating income +15.4% and margin -32bps; median company +20.3%, breadth 44/62
claims.obtained: own computation from yfinance quarterly financials
claims.why_load_bearing: Overturns a bearish economy-wide margin-collapse read that the aggregate alone supports. Establishes the standing rule that an Indian aggregate is never reported without its median and breadth.
claims.note: Three loss-makers are 26.6% of sample revenue with a combined operating loss of Rs7,776cr. Not comparable to the FY26 4.5% net figure -- different period, different measure, different universe.

claims.claim: S&P 500 translated to INR beat the Nifty in 97% of 108 rolling 10-year windows, 92% of 5-year and 72% of 3-year, mean gap ~4.5-4.8pp/yr; every calendar sub-period 2008-2026 favours the S&P in rupees
claims.obtained: own computation, 228 months of monthly data from 2007-09
claims.why_load_bearing: Undercuts the framing premise of this entire workspace. An India-specific book must clear a ~4.5pp/yr structural headwind versus a passive foreign alternative, and with 4 of 30 theses scored there is no evidence yet that it does.
claims.note: Not tested against an equal-weight or ex-mega-cap S&P, which is the obvious first challenge. 2023-2026 gap of +15.23pp is driven by US mega-cap concentration.

claims.claim: Every $10/bbl on crude widens India's CAD by ~$16.7bn (India Ratings) and adds ~60bp to inflation (CareEdge); crude sustained at $80 adds ~0.4pp CPI and 0.3-0.5% of GDP to the CAD (Moneycontrol)
claims.obtained: agent research, cross-checked against own computation
claims.why_load_bearing: Sizes every oil scenario for India. Independently confirms the $16-20bn/yr figure computed here from assumed 4.5-5.5 mb/d imports -- two methods, same answer.
claims.source: India Ratings via BW Businessworld 2026-03-31; CareEdge via ET 2026-03-30
claims.note: Own bottom-up estimate was $16-20bn per $10. India Ratings says $16.7bn. Agreement across independent methods.

claims.claim: The Russian crude discount fully eroded and inverted to a PREMIUM during 2026: Urals topped Brent in the Indian market for the first time (Reuters 2026-03-06), delivered Urals neared $100 (Mar), 'strong demand flips Russian Urals to premium' (2026-08-21)
claims.why_load_bearing: India is carrying the Senate-sanctions tail risk -- a 100% tariff threat that passed the Senate 86-11 -- for a discount that no longer exists. The strategic cost is being paid and the economic benefit is gone.
claims.note: No source gives a current $/bbl premium figure. Unresolved.

claims.claim: Samsung Electronics + SK Hynix are 55.5% of KOSPI market cap, up from 22% at end-2023. Ex those two, KOSPI forward P/E was 12x (UBS, May 2026). KOSPI blended P/E is at its lowest since 2008 despite the index doubling, because those two companies' earnings grew faster than their prices.
claims.why_load_bearing: Buying 'Korea' is buying two memory stocks. And a blended P/E at a 2008 low on doubled prices is the arithmetic of a cyclical peak stated as a valuation virtue.
claims.source: UBS via agent research; multiple outlets

claims.claim: SK Hynix Q2 2026: revenue KRW79.3tn (+257% YoY), operating profit ~KRW60.5tn (+557% YoY), 76% operating margin -- and the stock FELL ~10% on the print (Reuters, 2026-07-29, 'record profit misses forecasts')
claims.obtained: agent research, cross-checked against own income-statement pull
claims.why_load_bearing: A 557% profit print that loses a tenth of the company's value in a day is the cleanest available evidence that expectations have outrun even spectacular delivery. Confirms the cyclical-top read.

claims.claim: BOJ raised to 1.0% on 2026-06-16 (31-year high), yen short positioning hit a nine-year high around that decision, and Japan and the US executed a rare JOINT FX intervention to support the yen on 2026-08-02/03. Foreign ownership of Japanese equities at a record above one third, $60bn bought in H1 2026.
claims.why_load_bearing: A hiking central bank plus a nine-year-high short base plus joint intervention are the three ingredients of a carry unwind, which does not stay in Japan. India is not insulated by being uninvolved.
claims.source: Reuters/CNBC/Al Jazeera on the intervention; CoinDesk on positioning
claims.note: Intervention size not reconciled: Y5tn / $36.58bn / $46.9bn.

claims.claim: OBBBA imposes a 1% excise tax on remittances effective 2026-01-01, with carve-outs for bank-account-funded transfers, crypto, military transfers and sub-$15 transfers
claims.obtained: peer agent research; ONE non-primary source (Wikipedia). India-specific application, wire-vs-cash scope, visa-status distinctions and enforcement status as of Aug 2026 all NOT FOUND.
claims.why_load_bearing: The US is India's largest remittance source at 27.7%, and remittances are the largest stabilising inflow India has. But the bank-account-funded carve-out is the channel most India remittances actually use, so this may DEFUSE rather than confirm the risk flagged in the Washington-concentration note.
claims.note: LOW CONFIDENCE. Single secondary source. Do not act on this without the statutory text. The carve-out scope is the whole question and it is unverified.

claims.claim: Reliance FY+1 EPS cut 5.23% in 30 days
claims.obtained: origin unknown -- appeared in this workspace without a source
claims.why_load_bearing: It is half of the stated tension in the Reliance thesis (promoter buying against falling estimates). If it is not real, the tension is not real either.
claims.note: Targeted search could not retrieve it. General downgrade headlines exist (Jan 2026 post-Q3, Jul 2026 post-Q1) but no matching percentage. Same shape as the ERP R-squared error: a specific, confident-sounding statistic with no locatable source. Do not lean on it in either direction. CONFIRMED NOT FOUND 2026-08-29 against sell-side, data-vendor and press sources. Real Reliance revisions exist (brokers cut FY25-27 EPS 3.3-9.5% in Oct 2024) but nothing matches 5.23%/30 days. Stays buried.

claims.claim: RBI approved Sandeep Bakhshi's reappointment through 2028 on 22-23 May 2026; the stock rallied 2%. All 'contested' coverage predates the approval.
claims.obtained: red-team agent research, five concordant outlets
claims.why_load_bearing: Corrects a live cap on a live position. The governance fight I capped ICICI for was resolved in the bank's favour three months before I capped it.
claims.source: Reuters / ET / Moneycontrol / BusinessLine / Business Today, 22-25 May 2026
claims.note: The separate 24 Aug Bhushan letter on employee governance is multi-bank and its SUBSTANCE IS UNKNOWN. That is the open item, not the reappointment.

claims.claim: NTPC CMD Gurdeep Singh received a SECOND extension in July 2026 running to January 2027, after 18 shortlisted candidates were interviewed without a successor being chosen; the search dates to at least Oct 2024
claims.why_load_bearing: Re-specifies the NTPC risk. A selection process that has failed twice over ~22 months is a governance signal; the Rs35cr Ramagundam FIR I had been carrying is immaterial against >Rs1.8 lakh crore revenue.

claims.claim: India remittance inflows FY2024-25: US$135.46bn, a record, +14% YoY over FY2023-24's $118.7bn
claims.obtained: provisional RBI data via multiple outlets
claims.why_load_bearing: Sizes the largest single stabilising inflow India has, and settles the $145bn figure this base could not previously reconcile.

claims.claim: Prashant Bhushan representation to the RBI Governor dated 22 Aug 2026 alleging employee-governance failures at ICICI and Axis -- coercive resignations, and ~782 ICICI employees listed before labour authorities as having 'stopped reporting'. Copied to MoF, MCA, Labour Ministry, Chief Labour Commissioner, NHRC, PAC and SEBI.
claims.why_load_bearing: This is the sole remaining reason the ICICI position is capped. It is NOT the low-substance complaint that would have lifted the cap -- it carries specific statutory sections and a checkable headline number.
claims.note: NO RBI response, acknowledgement or enforcement step found. Media pickup confined to one small outlet five days on, while mainstream press covered the earlier reappointment matter heavily. Substance without traction, so far.

claims.claim: SEBI cleared the Jio Platforms DRHP on 2026-08-28; reported size Rs35,000-37,700cr (~$3.8-4bn). No listing date or price band yet.
claims.why_load_bearing: Materially de-risks the catalyst path for the Reliance SOTP thesis, whose written invalidation is a year-end listing deadline.

claims.claim: Reliance FY27 EPS was UPGRADED 7.4% (Rs56 -> Rs60) in recent sell-side notes; no evidence of any 5.23%/30-day cut
claims.obtained: agent research across sell-side, data vendors and press
claims.why_load_bearing: Removes the stated tension in the Reliance thesis. The 'promoter buying into falling estimates' framing rested on a figure that does not exist and the actual trend runs the other way.

claims.claim: RBI leadership refreshed in one window: DG Rohit Jain appointed 25 Aug (succeeding T. Rabi Sankar, 3-yr term); DG Swaminathan Janakiraman reappointed for 2 years on 26 Aug; the Central Board turned over 5+ seats between 21-23 Aug
claims.why_load_bearing: Who holds the levers is a standing question in this base. A concentrated leadership refresh at the regulator that sets rates, runs the FX defence and rules on bank CEO appointments is a governance signal in its own right.

claims.claim: National rainfall deficit flat at 13-15% since late July, but deficient districts rose 69 -> 412 while kharif sowing recovered to 96% of normal and reservoirs sit above 60%. Regional concentration severe: AP -51%, Meghalaya -58%, Punjab -34%, Karnataka -31%
claims.why_load_bearing: Undercuts the national-binary framing of the rural trade. The headline aggregate and the ground indicators are moving independently.
claims.note: The 69->412 district jump rests on an unverified base figure. 'Weakest since 2009' remains an open question in the outlets that raised it, not settled.

claims.claim: Six independent Polymarket Fed contracts repriced toward a hike between 2026-08-27 and 2026-08-29: hike-by-October 0.445->0.595, hike-by-September 0.305->0.445, no-change-after-September 0.675->0.545, +25bp 0.305->0.435, and hike-in-2026 0.565->0.665
claims.obtained: own computation from two Polymarket snapshots stored by this repo
claims.why_load_bearing: Settles the FedWatch-vs-Jackson-Hole contradiction from 28 Aug -- the hawkishness IS in the price at ~44.5% for September, up from 30.5%. Also confirms this base's contrarian rate-cycle-turned view, which is rarer than a correction and deserves the same scepticism.

claims.claim: Every Polymarket 'Iran blockade ends by X' contract fell across every tenor between 27 and 29 Aug (Sep 7 0.115->0.045 through Dec 31 0.706->0.664); Hormuz-normalisation odds fell with them
claims.why_load_bearing: The market is pricing the disruption as more persistent. This base holds that only SUPPLY shocks hurt India -- the Nifty fell in all four large ones of the last decade. But WTI fell 3.95% the same week, so rising blockade-persistence against falling crude is an unresolved tension, not a confirmation.

claims.claim: Kevin Warsh is the sitting Chair of the Federal Reserve, chairing the FOMC as a permanent voting member; reportedly confirmed to the Board 51-45 on 2026-05-12
claims.why_load_bearing: Decides whether his 28 Aug Jackson Hole hawkishness is policy signal or commentary. It is the Chair, so it is signal -- and that is the piece that makes the whole Fed picture cohere.
claims.note: The 51-45 confirmation vote is reported and not independently cross-checked.

claims.claim: Federal funds target range is 3.50-3.75%, per the July 28-29 2026 FOMC statement. The 3.75-4.00% figure in circulation had no live source.

July 28-29 2026 FOMC voted 9-3 to hold. Dissenters: Beth Hammack (Cleveland), Neel Kashkari (Minneapolis), Lorie Logan (Dallas). PCE at 3.7%, well above the 2% target; Warsh called inflation the Committee's predominant focus.
claims.obtained: FOMC statement and Jackson Hole remarks
claims.why_load_bearing: Sources a claim this base had been asserting. Combined with the odds repricing, every Fed input now points the same way.

claims.claim: ICICIBANK's -1.23% on 2026-08-28 has a multiply-sourced same-day explanation: bond pricing and an ESOP allotment. Neither is a negative story.
claims.why_load_bearing: Withdraws a weak inference linking the decline to the Bhushan governance letter.

claims.claim: India repo rate 5.25% (VERIFIED from rbi.org.in directly), bank rate 5.50%, CRR 3.00%, SLR 18.00%. Held four straight MPC meetings; last move the 6 Dec 2025 cut; next MPC 7 Oct 2026. System liquidity in SURPLUS -- RBI ran ~Rs3.4-4.0 lakh crore of VRRR absorptions with a further Rs3 lakh crore scheduled 31 Aug. 10y G-sec at a two-month high ~6.85-6.91%.
claims.why_load_bearing: This base has leaned on the G-sec yield for its ERP work and on a rate view, without ever recording the actual repo rate, the liquidity stance or the curve. VRRR absorption means surplus, not deficit -- easy to invert.
claims.source: rbi.org.in front page, fetched directly 2026-08-29 (rates); remainder agent-reported
claims.note: The policy corridor is now VERIFIED from RBI's own site via scripts/fetch_india_primary.py. The liquidity, MPC-history and G-sec figures remain REPORTED -- they live in Bulletin tables on rbidocs.rbi.org.in, which serves a TSPD JavaScript challenge and cannot be fetched without a JS-executing browser.

claims.claim: System non-food credit growth 15.8-20% across 2026 readings, but deposit growth 14.7% and decelerating faster -- a 4-5pp gap, credit-deposit ratio at a record ~83% (March), system NIM compressing 5bp YoY to 3.21% (June). Asset quality improving: system GNPA 2.1%, a multi-decadal low; SBI GNPA 2.13%->1.47%, NNPA 0.53%->0.38% since Sep 2024. Fastest-growing retail book is gold-loan-heavy, 42.4% CAGR since Mar 2024, and RBI's own FSR flags gold-price volatility as a risk.
claims.why_load_bearing: Re-specifies the SBI invalidation. The risk was written as deceleration toward 12%; the actual live risk is a funding gap at a record CD ratio with NIM compressing. Different trigger, different watch.

claims.claim: IIP decelerated to +6.7% YoY in July from a revised +8.8% in June; manufacturing PMI flash 52.9 in August, the weakest improvement since Aug 2021, with manufacturing EMPLOYMENT contracting for the first time in 2.5 years; e-way bill volume growth +6% YoY in July against +14.5% in June while GST value growth accelerated to +15.4%
claims.why_load_bearing: Sits against the capex-over-consumption spread that has been widening for six months. If real activity is softening while the capex trade works, the spread is a rotation and not a cycle -- which is the exact question this base said it could not answer.
claims.note: The GST acceleration is confounded by GST 2.0 base effects and should not be read as a clean demand signal. The volume-vs-value divergence is the more honest read.

claims.claim: IIP July use-based headline says capital goods surge while consumer non-durables contract, and Q2 peak power demand hit a record 270.8 GW (+12% YoY) -- but the power record is attributed to heatwave AC load not industrial, and Manufacturing PMI flash is 52.9, weakest since Aug 2021, with manufacturing employment contracting for the first time in 2.5 years
claims.why_load_bearing: The capex-over-consumption spread has widened for six months and this base could not say whether it was a cycle or a rotation. The evidence splits along lagging-index versus forward-survey, which is a real distinction and not noise to be averaged.
claims.note: The actual IIP capital-goods percentage was never retrieved -- only the headline phrase. That single number would settle it.

claims.claim: Measured 2026-08-29: www.rbi.org.in, www.mospi.gov.in, eaindustry.nic.in, www.fbil.org.in, www.nsdl.co.in and data.rbi.org.in all return HTTP 200 to a request with a browser User-Agent. rbidocs.rbi.org.in (the document host) serves an Imperva/TSPD JavaScript challenge for every PDF/DOC. www.cmegroup.com returns 403.
claims.why_load_bearing: Agent reports repeatedly tiered Indian macro figures as `reported` on the grounds that primary sources were unreachable. For the HTML pages that was wrong, and a whole category of verifiable data was being downgraded for no reason. But the document host IS genuinely challenge-protected, which is what actually blocks the Bulletin's statistical tables.
claims.note: 'The site is blocked' and 'this host is blocked' are different claims. Collapsing them cost a real capability -- and an agent that said rbidocs specifically was TSPD-protected on 2026-08-27 was exactly right.

claims.claim: 'Indian consensus earnings missed for nine consecutive years' -- NO SOURCE FOUND after 15+ targeted searches including exact phrases and named analysts (Kotak's Prasad, Motilal Oswal, Marcellus, Chris Wood)
claims.why_load_bearing: This base asserted it as settled fact in its load-bearing list, position notes and earnings framing. RETIRED means stop repeating it -- not disproved, per this base's own rule that not_found is a statement about the search.
claims.note: Replaced by the narrower dated version: a ~9% cumulative FY27 EPS downgrade cycle hitting 62-66% of Nifty constituents through spring 2026, now turned.

claims.claim: Stablecoin supply $311.3bn on 2026-08-29, +1.3% YTD and +10.3% YoY, growing MONOTONICALLY through an Oct 2025 - Jun 2026 crash that took BTC -53% and ETH -67% peak-to-trough. BTC $77,949 (-11% YTD), ETH $2,444.50 (-17.7% YTD). DeFi TVL -42.5% YoY, moving in lockstep with price.
claims.obtained: CoinGecko and DefiLlama APIs fetched directly
claims.why_load_bearing: Evidences a framing this base asserted without support -- stablecoin supply as a real-capital proxy versus price. The two series decoupled across a 53-67% drawdown, so the crash was a de-rating rather than capital flight. Also establishes that DeFi TVL is mark-to-market and NOT a flow signal.
claims.source: CoinGecko /simple/price and market_chart; DefiLlama stablecoins and TVL endpoints

claims.claim: Only an ISSUE SIZE is public for the Jio Platforms IPO (Rs35,000-38,000cr / ~$3.8-4.1bn). No implied equity valuation is company- or filing-confirmed. The single circulating valuation ($128bn) is a pre-filing June brokerage estimate with unknown methodology and unnamed banks -- and it sits BELOW this base's prior $130-180bn SOTP range.
claims.why_load_bearing: The Reliance SOTP thesis is anchored to this listing and has NO public equity-value peg. The one number that exists points the wrong way for the thesis. A price band typically lands 1-3 weeks pre-listing; until then the anchor does not exist.

claims.claim: July 2026 AMFI: small-cap funds took the single largest equity inflow of any category (Rs7,767cr) while large-cap funds were in OUTFLOW (-Rs1,321cr). But only 37% of Smallcap 250 names beat the index over the past year -- an 8-year low -- even as the index sits near highs. Liquidity is NOT stressed: stress tests show 11 days to liquidate half a book, improved from 15-18 days a year ago. Q1 FY27 PAT growth accelerates down the cap curve: large +18-21%, mid +23%, small +31-38%.
claims.why_load_bearing: This base held that SIP flows are a structural bid most fragile in small caps. The flow-concentration half is confirmed; the fragility half rests on the WRONG mechanism -- liquidity is improving, not deteriorating. The real tell is narrowing breadth at an 8-year low.
claims.source: AMFI July 2026 data via agent research
